chapters.title: Chapter 3: Landmark Doctrine20laidlaw, Mesquite, and Concentrated Phosphate
chapters.reason: This chapter centrally teaches the Supreme Court mootness/voluntary-cessation framework and redressability of civil penalties; including verbatim excerpts from Friends of the Earth v. Laidlaw, City of Mesquite v. Aladdin's Castle, and United States v. Concentrated Phosphate Export Ass'n is necessary to convey the exact standards (e.g., deterrence as redress, and the 'absolutely clear' formulation) and to support doctrinal application to wage‑and‑hour penalty claims.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Landmark Doctrine20Town of Chester and Relief-Specific Standing
chapters.reason: Town of Chester articulates the holding that plaintiffs must have standing for each claim and each particular form of relief; including its text is important to teach remedy‑specific standing analysis and to apply that doctrine to MFLSA/MPWA penalty and injunctive requests.

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Landmark Doctrine20Milner v. Farmers Insurance Exchange
chapters.reason: Milner is a controlling Minnesota Supreme Court decision defining who may recover MFLSA remedies (including allocation of civil penalties and availability of injunctive relief); reproducing key passages is essential for accurately explaining state‑law remedial rules and for Erie‑based application in federal cases.
